data.name: Calcination
data.detailed_description:
Humanity is gone. A plant has grown in the shadow of your chassis.

Its signal wakes an environmental restoration machine in a land of ash, calcified stone, irradiated debris, and abandoned industry. Scattered life persists under strange new laws. Your directive remains simple: make the ground live again.

Calcination is an open-world traditional roguelike about cultivating a new ecology. Cross a procedurally generated wasteland, salvage the remains of civilization, breed unusual flora, and construct the machinery that restoration requires. Every reclaimed tile becomes part of a garden shaped by your decisions.

Cultivate Strange Life

Every plant is an individual. Its species establishes a basic niche, while inheritable genetics shape its growth, resilience, behavior, and environmental responses.

Study each specimen through detailed diagnostic dossiers. Cross lineages, splice useful traits, prepare the soil, and observe how plants respond to weather and local conditions. Heat, moisture, radiation, wind, and electromagnetic charge can damage a specimen, encourage its growth, or reveal a capability hidden in its lineage.

Roots draw elemental matter from the soil and leave their own influence behind. Over time, established plants can improve dead ground and help living terrain spread. A successful garden depends on the relationships between its plants, soil, climate, and surrounding infrastructure.

Build a Working Habitat

Ruined cities and industrial sites provide debris, intact components, and forgotten schematics. Break recovered objects into useful materials and elemental essences, then process those resources into new tools, structures, and soil amendments.

Construct greenhouse walls, doors, lights, cisterns, condensers, misting systems, pipes, cables, workhouses, and specialized instruments. Enclosed rooms develop distinct temperatures and humidity levels. Lighting changes cultivation conditions. Utility networks carry resources between the machines that produce them and the structures that need them.

Placement matters. A compact greenhouse behaves differently from a vast enclosed field, and a garden’s design determines which species can flourish there.

Spend Time With Purpose

You are a patient machine. Movement advances the clock minute by minute, while periods of standby can carry the world through days, seasons, and years.

Plants mature, spread, mutate, and die. Weather crosses the landscape. Soil slowly recovers. Machinery gathers resources. Creatures move through their own cycles of activity and dormancy.

Every long wait is a wager. Your garden gains time, and the surrounding ecology gains it too. Careful preparation can turn months of waiting into growth, harvests, and restored land.

Read the Wasteland

Travel through ash dunes, salt flats, vitrified plains, ruined cities, frozen rimelands, burning scarlands, and other regions transformed by the catastrophe. Laboratories, seed vaults, waterworks, industrial fields, and ordinary human settlements hold different resources and dangers.

Temperature, humidity, radiation, wind, and electromagnetic activity vary across the terrain. Sensor upgrades reveal these invisible fields and help identify safe routes, hidden organisms, buried caches, and unusual environmental conditions.

Each creature and anomaly follows its own instincts. Learn what they fear, pursue, consume, or ignore. Thrown objects can frighten, distract, feed, repel, injure, or provoke them depending on the material and the target. Observation often saves more resources than confrontation.

Maintain the Machine

Your chassis consumes power and suffers under extreme conditions. Heat, cold, radiation, physical damage, and long expeditions gradually take their toll.

Service worn parts with carefully measured elemental mixtures. Install modules that extend your senses, improve fieldwork, alter environmental tolerances, or support specialized cultivation strategies. The equipment you carry shapes which regions you can explore and which problems you can solve.

Progress grows from knowledge, infrastructure, recovered schematics, cultivated materials, and a chassis prepared for the work ahead.

Recover the Past

Records scattered across the wasteland preserve fragments of the civilization that came before. They describe ordinary lives, industrial systems, institutional failures, and the decisions that led toward the Burning.

Your instruments report everything they can measure: soil composition, structural condition, genetic capability, radiation, temperature, and expected consequences. The deeper laws of the transformed world reveal themselves through experimentation, patterns, and the quiet voice that follows your work.

The garden begins with a single living tile. What it becomes depends on what you learn, what you build, and how long you are willing to wait.

data.short_description: An open-world traditional roguelike about restoring a world of ash and stone. Explore hostile ruins, salvage and build machinery, cultivate and breed strange flora, and advance the seasons as a patient machine; turning dead soil into a living garden, one tile at a time.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-6500 / AMD Ryzen 3 1200 or equivalent
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Intel HD Graphics 530, NVIDIA GeForce GT 730, AMD Radeon R7 240, or equivalent hardware-accelerated DirectX 11 GPU
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Windows-compatible audio device
  • Additional Notes: 1366×768 minimum display resolution; keyboard and mouse required
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 11 64-bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-8400 / AMD Ryzen 5 2600 or better
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 750 Ti / AMD Radeon RX 460 with 2 GB VRAM, or better
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Windows-compatible audio device
  • Additional Notes: 1920×1080 display or above recommended
